# Source access for recipients

Prepared 2026-11-05 for the exact versions in `provenance.json` and [the source ledger](remote-sources.json). Original Read Aloud files remain MIT. The combined application includes GPL-covered code and preserves recipients' applicable GPL rights; the MIT label is not a license for every bundled component.

## Get the source

1. Open the [public Read Aloud repository](https://github.com/Fidasek009/read-aloud). Select the tag matching the installed release, then download that tag's source archive. No store reviewer account, payment or request to the publisher is required. This supplies our preferred TypeScript source, packaging changes, Bun lockfile, build instructions and preserved third-party sources/build recipes under `vendor/`.
2. Obtain the full Spellophone, eSpeak NG and WXT source archives listed in [README.md](README.md). Their SHA-256 values and exact revisions are recorded there and in `provenance.json`. The README explains the dictionary patch, pronunciation-data rename and supplier build relationship.
3. For the other bundled code, use the pinned preferred-source archive links below and the exact dependency archive URLs/checksums in `remote-sources.json`. The `recipes/` directory preserves the relevant supplier files unchanged, with `.txt` appended to each filename. Strip that suffix when placing those files into an extracted supplier tree. Full upstream trees contain additional source, headers, scripts and license files.
4. Build the extension with the Bun procedure in [`SOURCE_CODE_REVIEW.md`](../../SOURCE_CODE_REVIEW.md). Rebuilding upstream native dependencies is separate from building our extension from the pinned published packages. The supplier reference scripts describe their own Python/CMake/Emscripten/Rust/JavaScript tooling; they do not introduce a Node requirement for this project's toolchain.

This uses the equivalent-source-access mechanism in [GPLv3 section 6(d)](https://www.gnu.org/licenses/gpl-3.0.html#section6), including clearly identified third-party servers. Maintainers remain responsible for keeping the required source available while conveying the binaries; a broken upstream URL must be repaired or mirrored. A private Firefox reviewer ZIP is not a substitute for recipient access. Source can be on a different server, as explained in the [FSF source-access FAQ](https://www.gnu.org/licenses/gpl-faq.en.html#SourceAndBinaryOnDifferentSites).

## ONNX Runtime Web 1.31.1

Get [full ORT source at `6af1a932…`](https://codeload.github.com/microsoft/onnxruntime/tar.gz/6af1a932e2286d5c58166085d24c68783033edee). Preferred JavaScript/TypeScript source is in `js/web/lib` and `js/common/lib`; native code is in `onnxruntime/`, `include/` and `cmake/`. `js/web/script/build.ts` defines the published JavaScript variants, and the web/common package locks pin the supplier's JavaScript dependencies. The source ledger gives their resolved source packages and integrity values, including separate preferred FlatBuffers TypeScript source. Installed transitive packages need not be the versions already compiled into the supplier's minified bundles.

Our CPU worker uses `ort.wasm.min.mjs` and `ort-wasm-simd-threaded.{mjs,wasm}`. Our GPU worker uses `ort.webgpu.min.mjs` and `ort-wasm-simd-threaded.asyncify.{mjs,wasm}`. The selected files and their SHA-256 values are recorded in the ledger; `scripts/prepare-runtime.ts` records our bundling/copying steps.

The preserved `linux-wasm-ci.yml`, `onnxruntime_webassembly.cmake` and WebGPU CMake files define these supplier targets. The shared build options are `--config Release --build_wasm --enable_wasm_simd --enable_wasm_threads`; the WebGPU target adds `--use_webgpu --use_webnn`, the `onnxruntime_webassembly` target and the reduced-operator/type configuration. Use the complete preserved recipe for its remaining options and generated glue inputs. Native linking includes ORT core/CPU providers/MLAS plus configured ONNX, protobuf, flatbuffers, re2 and header dependencies. Emscripten's WebGPU build uses Dawn's `emdawnwebgpu` bridge and generated API interfaces; it does not incorporate all desktop Dawn GPU drivers.

`cmake/deps.txt` gives the supplier archive URLs and SHA-1 pins. `cmake/external/onnxruntime_external_deps.cmake` determines selection and applies the preserved date/GSL/ONNX patches. Relevant pins include ONNX 1.22.0, native FlatBuffers 23.5.26 and Dawn `v20260916.214021`; the complete file retains conditional dependencies without claiming all are linked. The ONNX git submodule is not automatically the selected source: default FetchContent builds use the ONNX archive from `deps.txt`.

The supplier pipeline selects Emscripten SDK **4.0.23**. [Full Emscripten source at `7a5d93b5…`](https://codeload.github.com/emscripten-core/emscripten/tar.gz/7a5d93b50f6a3a35e85a0d2fc9e667b8498e6aed), including `src/` and `system/lib`, supplies generated JavaScript/runtime-library source. Exact emsdk/other gitlinks are recorded in the ledger. The Spellophone supplier separately selects **6.0.12**, whose [full source](https://codeload.github.com/emscripten-core/emscripten/tar.gz/5488e0871d46d19a3209988190fa6a653126256f) supplies its runtime family. Providing those sources avoids relying on a blanket assertion that all compiler runtime code is exempt. General-purpose compiler executables, tests and build-only dev dependencies are not automatically shipped components.

## PDF.js 6.5.438

Get [full PDF.js source at `0a415334…`](https://codeload.github.com/mozilla/pdf.js/tar.gz/0a4153349dc473ba950fc17941c5ca7eda43c1de). This is the published package's `gitHead`; its `src/`, `web/`, `external/`, build scripts and dependency lock supply the preferred first-party source. Installed decoder WASM files were compared by SHA-256 with the exact `external/` files at this revision. Their respective external READMEs identify Mozilla's separate wrapper/build repositories.

| Shipped decoder | Wrapper source and build recipe | Native source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| OpenJPEG | [Wrapper `d5f16ba3…`](https://codeload.github.com/mozilla/pdf.js.openjpeg/tar.gz/d5f16ba380391d4e32b51834e2e0afa796e402d8); `Dockerfile`, buffer-stream patch, `compile_lib.sh`, `compile.sh`, `src/` | [OpenJPEG `8314119b…`](https://codeload.github.com/uclouvain/openjpeg/tar.gz/8314119b067c0fc77834731168daaebd379fdb12), pinned in that Dockerfile. Apply the preserved patch before building. |
| JBIG2/CCITT | [Wrapper `15f6f935…`](https://codeload.github.com/mozilla/pdf.js.jbig2/tar.gz/15f6f9357c5e5e30285eb83aa08e5fe1a16ab77a); `compile.sh`, `src/`, `build/build*.h` | [PDFium `bb1f9f71…`](https://pdfium.googlesource.com/pdfium/+/bb1f9f71e7b15afdd5937adf8cfe5807522b882f/). `compile.sh` explicitly enumerates JBIG2/fax/scanline and supporting fxcrt/fxge translation units; it does not build the whole browser engine. |
| qcms | [Wrapper `2ae4ee72…`](https://codeload.github.com/mozilla/pdf.js.qcms/tar.gz/2ae4ee72334782928210ba4050e3e77d9b2d35be); `src/lib.rs`, `js/`, Cargo files and `compile.sh` | [qcms 0.3.0 source crate](https://static.crates.io/crates/qcms/qcms-0.3.0.crate), checksum in ledger. |
| QuickJS | [Wrapper `1b37671f…`](https://codeload.github.com/mozilla/pdf.js.quickjs/tar.gz/1b37671f1b529f887673f33ba4c5f00981a8065b); engine patch, `compile.sh`, `src/` | [QuickJS `3d5e064e…`](https://codeload.github.com/bellard/quickjs/tar.gz/3d5e064e9dd67c70f7962836505a7fa067bf0a4e), explicitly pinned by both the PDF update and wrapper Dockerfile. |

The PDF qcms update explicitly names its wrapper revision; the JBIG2 update and wrapper both name the PDFium revision. OpenJPEG/QuickJS wrapper revisions are inferred from the latest wrapper commit before the PDF binary update and matching source/recipe changes; the ledger preserves those evidence limits. Their native revisions are explicit Dockerfile pins. These mappings do not claim supplier-signed native-build attestations.

The qcms Dockerfile runs `cargo update`: its committed lock still says wasm-bindgen 0.2.100, while the shipped WASM's metadata and source paths identify **wasm-bindgen 0.2.126**, **Rust 1.97.1** at `8bab26f4f68e0e26f0bb7960be334d5b520ea452`, **qcms 0.3.0** and **dlmalloc 0.2.13**. Use the [actual wasm-bindgen source](https://codeload.github.com/wasm-bindgen/wasm-bindgen/tar.gz/21ac804a96c0c5c5d6459084686a9a17a8a3c865), [Rust standard/alloc library source and library/Cargo.lock](https://codeload.github.com/rust-lang/rust/tar.gz/8bab26f4f68e0e26f0bb7960be334d5b520ea452), and [dlmalloc source crate](https://static.crates.io/crates/dlmalloc/dlmalloc-0.2.13.crate) for these embedded runtime portions. Rust's library/Cargo.lock supplies registry source checksums; use pinned gitlinks recursively for any enabled submodule source. Walrus is a build transformation tool, not automatically embedded runtime code.

The other decoder Dockerfiles use `emscripten/emsdk:latest`, without a compiler-image digest. We preserve the actual supplier recipes and native sources, but do not invent an exact compiler version or updated cargo lock. These are supplier build-provenance/reproducibility limitations. GPL source delivery does not universally require exact compiler-output hashes, and this audit has not independently rebuilt upstream native artifacts.

No model weights, training recordings or preview audio are included in these source materials. Those integration scopes and terms are assessed separately in [`docs/licensing.md`](../../docs/licensing.md).
